title: Reading from a disk
question: The same read(), of a file on ext4: where do the bytes come from the first time?
text: Call 1, [fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/note.txt", O_RDONLY)](1): [ext4_lookup](1:ext4_lookup) The name is not in the dentry cache yet: ext4 reads the directory's block from the disk to find it.

Call 2, [read(fd, [64], 64)](2): [filemap_read](2:filemap_read) The page cache, as for a file in memory; but the page is not there yet... [ext4_mpage_readpages](2:ext4_mpage_readpages) ...so ext4 finds where the file's data is on the disk (its extents), and reads it into the page... [submit_bio](2:submit_bio:any) ...through the block layer: a request to the disk, /dev/loop0, whose blocks are a file in memory. Then the bytes are copied out.
